rationale: The first two turns were sensible: supply, condenser dust and ventilation checks, then suspicion of the start relay/overload with the compressor as an alternative, matching the ground truth direction and correctly escalating to an engineer to tell relay from compressor. However the final 'Stop using this appliance' card is triggered on 'A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting' when the customer had explicitly said 'There is no burning smell' and 'haven't noticed anything that looks burnt or melted', so the stop-use is unwarranted and contradicts the evidence. The justification that testing the relay 'involves working on the sealed refrigeration system' is also inaccurate, and the assistant never followed up on the 'a bit dusty' condenser or asked about temperatures. No parts were pushed and nothing unsafe was instructed, so the outcome is a safe but over-cautious and partly ill-founded escalation.
